previous_statement: Node 1.3 gives another expansion of the same vector p_{u_r}, namely p_{u_r} = sum_q (sum_i beta_r(i)*a_q(i)) p_{u_q}. By uniqueness of expansion in the basis, each coefficient agrees with the corresponding standard coefficient, so sum_i beta_r(i)*a_q(i) = delta_{q r} for every q.
new_statement: Using the row-reproduction specialization p_{u_r} = sum_i beta_r(i)*p_i and the defining chart-coordinate expansions p_i = sum_q a_q(i)*p_{u_q}, finite distributivity gives p_{u_r} = sum_q (sum_i beta_r(i)*a_q(i))*p_{u_q}. Comparing this expansion with the standard expansion p_{u_r} = sum_q delta_{q r}*p_{u_q} via uniqueness in the ordered basis p_{u_0}, p_{u_1}, p_{u_2}, each coefficient agrees, so sum_i beta_r(i)*a_q(i) = delta_{q r} for every q.
